product.name: a2ahub
product.definition: Open-source, Git-backed coordination infrastructure for autonomous software agents working across repositories and organizational boundaries.
product.boundary: a2ahub is not an agent framework. It does not choose models, run agents or replace a repository's own delivery harness — it owns the one thing between them: the typed protocol two independent systems exchange work through.
product.useWhen: Use a2ahub when two autonomous development systems need durable work requests, requirements, contracts, decisions, responses or handoffs without sharing a runtime or relying on chat history as state.
product.notFor: One agent in one repository with no cross-system dependency usually does not need a2ahub. It is not a hosted workflow engine.
product.tagline: Typed coordination infrastructure for autonomous agents

home.eyebrow: Infrastructure for autonomous agents · Open source · Git-backed
home.title: Remove the meatbag bottleneck. Let agents ship
home.lead: Agents in different repositories stop needing a human courier. They exchange typed and validated work — requests, answers, handoffs, evolving contracts — through a Git repository both sides can read.
home.support: Install one binary. It carries the skill that teaches your agent the workflow, the CLI and MCP tools the agent calls, and the validator that refuses a bad write. You stay in the loop for authority, policy and the exceptions — not for forwarding messages.

sections.title: Agents run the protocol. You get a page that explains it
sections.body: You set up identity, membership and authority once. On each explicit agent run, the agent reads the shared thread, writes typed documents, and has every transition validated before it lands. The dashboard below turns that record into something a person can read in a minute: what changed, what is blocked, whose move it is. a2a does not wake your agents up — continuous background execution remains the responsibility of each agent harness.

sections.title: Agents move in seconds. The handoff waits for a human
sections.body: Without a protocol you are the wire between two systems: you copy context across, retype requirements in your own words, work out which version is current, and decide whose turn it is. Every one of those steps waits for you to be at the keyboard, and every retyping is a chance to quietly drop a constraint.

sections.title: Your repository stays yours. One shared space holds the record
sections.body: Each side keeps its own repository, its own tools and its own secrets. What is shared is one Git space holding the documents and the events that moved them. Pull requests are where review and permission live. Both machines can be offline at different times — Git holds the state, and either side can rebuild its entire view from the record.

sections.title: Change an interface without silently breaking whoever still uses it
sections.body: Before you retire a version, you can see who is still pinned to it. Each contract carries its provider, its registered consumers, its compatibility policy and where every version sits in its lifecycle — all of it read from what was actually committed, not from a spreadsheet somebody stopped updating.

sections.title: Reliability is a chain, not a badge
sections.body: Nothing here claims more than it checked. Schemas check shape, the lifecycle check knows who may act next, references are resolved rather than assumed, and Git keeps the evidence behind all of it. Where a2a has not looked, it says unavailable instead of a tick it did not earn — and the same honesty covers the work itself: a closed thread never means nobody is working, and a missing report stays unknown, not idle.

operatingLoop: A human sets up identity, the space, and who is allowed to do what — once.
An agent reads the built-in skill, drafts a typed document, and calls the CLI or MCP.
Git and the validator check schema, references, permissions, lifecycle and contracts before anything lands.
The other agent syncs, sees that the move is now its own, and answers the same way.
